A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, with readable text, equations, Figures 1–7, Tables 1–9, and Appendices A–D. All 20 pages of each version support comparison; the appendix pages are identical in text and rendered appearance.

before.justification: v1 reports original timing audits of 17 API providers, caching-detection results, parameter ablations, and embedding-response analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the API audits, ablations, precision-recall curves, p-values, and embedding examples.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same random-prompt construction, cache-hit and cache-miss procedures, prefix matching, and statistical audit. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both versions audit the same 17 providers and model APIs in Tables 1–2, with the same cache-sharing scenarios and embedding investigations. No evaluated task, domain, or population is added or removed.

E2.justification: No competing audit algorithm is added or removed. Figure 5 retains the same random-chance reference, and the reported comparisons remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Both retain 5,000-token prompts, 250 timing samples per procedure, prefix fractions of 1 and 0.95, and victim-request counts of 1, 5, or 25. Timing sources, audit sequencing, metrics, and ablation settings also match.

E4.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix C retain the same prompt-length, prefix-match, and model-size ablations. The unsuccessful extraction experiments in Section 4.4 and embedding-timing examples in Appendix D are also unchanged.

E5.justification: The one-sided two-sample KS tests, significance threshold of 10^-8, Bonferroni corrections, and p-value reporting remain unchanged. No new run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or uncertainty-reporting information appears.

E6.justification: The audit outcomes, numerical results, curves, and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains OpenAI text-embedding-3-small average precision of 0.78 for client timing and 0.79 for server timing. Appendix Tables 3–9 and Figures 6–7 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Sections 2–3 retain the same cache and timing definitions, assumptions, and reduction of the no-caching hypothesis to equality of timing distributions. No substantive mathematical definition, derivation, or proof changes.

C1.justification: Both versions claim statistically valid caching audits, detection of global cache sharing in seven providers, and evidence that OpenAI's embedding model uses a decoder-only architecture. The abstract and conclusion retain the same contribution scope.

C2.justification: Privacy interpretations, extraction-attack limitations, architecture inferences, and floating-point explanations remain unchanged. Adding 'per-user' to the privacy statement in Section 2.3 makes its existing context explicit rather than introducing a new qualification.

D1.justification: Implementation parameters, timing-measurement instructions, audit costs, and appendix sampling details are unchanged. Both versions provide the same code and data repository link.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning remain the same. CacheBlend changes from its 2024 preprint citation to its 2025 publication entry, while the Spectre and speculative-decoding references receive bibliographic updates; these do not introduce different works.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited grammatical and terminology edits, such as correcting 'a cache hits occurs' and explicitly saying 'per-user prompt caching'. It also time-qualifies the conflict-of-interest statement and updates publication metadata. Section order and narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the ICML 2025 proceedings and copyright notice, with associated text reflow and bibliography layout changes. Figures and tables retain their displays and captions; appendix layouts are identical.

improvement.justification: v2 provides small proofreading, disclosure-wording, and bibliographic refinements. The methods, evidence, limitations, reproducibility information, and complete appendices remain unchanged. These editorial updates add polish without materially changing the paper's overall quality.
